name: REST OAI-PMH
description: Exposes entities as Dublin Core in an OAI-PMH endpoint using Views, REST, and a metadata mapping module of your choice.

suggests.discoverygarden/dgi_image_discovery: Provides image discovery support for RDF thumbnail URL callbacks.

provides_base_classes: Drupal\rest_oai_pmh\Plugin\OaiMetadataMapBase (abstract; build() renders a Twig template into an OAI metadata record)
Drupal\rest_oai_pmh\Plugin\OaiCacheBase (abstract; clearCache() reacts to entity CUD to keep the index fresh)
ecosystem_note: Publishes Drupal content as a standards-compliant OAI-PMH 2.0 repository at /oai/request (path configurable). It does NOT expose entities directly: you select one or more Views (each an 'Entity Reference' display) on the settings form; a cron/queue/batch job walks those Views and materializes an index in three DB tables (rest_oai_pmh_record, rest_oai_pmh_set, rest_oai_pmh_member). Each selected View becomes an OAI 'set' (or, if the display has an entity-reference contextual filter, each referenced entity becomes a set). At harvest time the OaiPmh REST resource plugin (id oai_pmh) answers the six OAI verbs (Identify, ListMetadataFormats, ListSets, ListIdentifiers, ListRecords, GetRecord) by querying the index, loading each entity, and running it through a configured OaiMetadataMap plugin (Dublin Core via RDF or Metatag, MODS, or raw). Access is re-checked live per entity (entity->access('view')) and per field (fieldItemList->access()) as the requesting user, so unpublished/unprivileged content in an indexed View is filtered out at request time. The endpoint is a normal REST resource: enabling the module installs it but a bare install returns 403 until the 'restful get oai_pmh' permission is granted (typically to anonymous, since OAI harvesters are anonymous). Two pluggable subsystems: OaiMetadataMap (how a Drupal entity becomes an XML metadata record) and OaiCache (liberal vs conservative index-invalidation strategy). Resumption tokens (paging) are stored in the rest_oai_pmh.resumption_token keyvalue store and expire after a configurable number of seconds.
